title: Payroll Clerk & Accounts Assistant
description:
Payroll Clerk & Accounts Assistant

Location: Caistor

Full Time

Monday to Friday 9:00am - 4:30pm

Manpower are currently recruiting for a Payroll Clerk & Accounts Assistant on behalf of our client. This is an excellent opportunity to join a well-established business where you'll play a key role in supporting payroll, accounts and administration functions within a close-knit and friendly team.

If you're an organised and detail-focused individual with payroll experience and a background in accounts support, we'd love to hear from you.

The Role

As a Payroll Clerk & Accounts Assistant, you'll be responsible for ensuring payroll is processed accurately and on time, whilst also providing support across the wider finance function.

Key Responsibilities
- Process weekly and monthly payroll accurately and within deadlines
- Maintain and update employee payroll records
- Check timesheets, holiday records, sickness absence and payroll data
- Respond to payroll-related queries from employees
- Process new starters and leavers
- Assist with pension administration and payroll submissions
- Prepare payroll reports and maintain payroll documentation
- Process employee expenses
- Process purchase and sales invoices
- Support accounts payable and accounts receivable activities
- Assist with general office administration duties
- Provide additional support to the finance team as required

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous payroll experience (essential)
- Experience within an accounts or bookkeeping environment
- Strong understanding of payroll processes and confidentiality requirements
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational and time management skills
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Office applications
- Experience using Sage Payroll and Sage Accounts (desirable)
- Ability to work independently and manage competing deadlines
- Strong communication and problem-solving skills
- A professional, positive and team-focused attitude

What's in it for You?
- Competitive salary of £27,000 - £34,000, dependent on experience
- Monday to Friday working hours, 9:00am - 4:30pm
- Paid 30-minute lunch break
- 22 days annual leave, plus an additional day off for your birthday
- Extra time off over Christmas while working within a skeleton staff rota
- Early finish at 12:30pm every other Friday
- Join a supportive team of just three people, where your contribution will be highly valued
- Laptop provided for office use
- Free onsite parking

Apply Today

If you're a dependable and trustworthy payroll professional looking for a varied role within a supportive and friendly team, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now or contact the Manpower team for more information.

If you receive suspicious outreach claiming to be from us, please contact us via the ManpowerGroup website.

title: Goods In Administrator
description:
Goods In Administrator

Location: Scunthorpe
Hours: 8:30am until 4:30pm Monday to Friday
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience

About the Company

Our client is a well-established, family-owned business operating within the UK steel distribution and processing industry, with over 160 years of heritage.

Operating across 29 sites throughout the UK and Ireland, the business holds more than 120,000 tonnes of steel stock and has built an outstanding reputation for delivering quality products and exceptional customer service.

Despite its significant size and presence within the industry, the business remains committed to its people, customers and local communities. Continued investment in employees, modern processing machinery, technology and materials-handling equipment ensures the business remains at the forefront of the industry.

This is a forward-thinking organisation that values hard work, ambition, teamwork and fresh ideas, offering an excellent opportunity to join a business where people genuinely matter.

About the Role

We are currently recruiting for an experienced Goods In Administrator to join a friendly and supportive team within a busy warehouse and manufacturing environment.

This is a varied administrative position, providing essential support across the Goods In and wider operations functions. The successful candidate will play an important role in ensuring incoming materials are accurately received, recorded and processed, whilst also providing general administrative and customer service support.

The role would suit someone who is highly organised, has excellent attention to detail and enjoys working in a busy environment where no two days are the same.

Key Responsibilities
- Answer incoming telephone calls, directing enquiries to the appropriate departments or individuals.
- Welcome visitors and assist with their movements whilst onsite.
- Process stock amendments as required, including printing and checking stock adjustment reports.
- Raise and process invoices, purchase orders and goods receipting notes.
- Manage incoming emails, responding appropriately or forwarding to the relevant departments.
- Ensure the accurate and efficient receipt of incoming materials in line with Goods Inwards schedules and procedures.
- Check test certifications and material documentation, ensuring all material standards and requirements are maintained.
- Carry out regular stock checks, identifying and correcting any discrepancies.
- Monitor incoming stock rotations, ensuring materials are presented with the correct colour coding and cast numbers.
- Ensure cut confirmation records are accurate and communicated to the relevant teams.
- Liaise with operational colleagues regarding daily work plans and priorities.
- Provide scanning, filing and general warehouse administrative support.
- Communicate professionally with internal and external customers via telephone and email.
- Support excellent customer service standards and contribute towards a continuous improvement culture.

Skills & Experience

The ideal candidate will have:
- Previous experience in an administrative role, ideally within goods in, manufacturing, warehousing, logistics or a similar environment.
- Excellent organisational skills and strong attention to detail.
- Confident verbal and written communication skills.
- A professional and friendly telephone manner.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and the ability to learn new systems.

What's on Offer?
- Highly competitive salary, dependent on experience.
- 25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays.
- Cycle to Work scheme.
- Life Assurance.
- Company discount scheme, offering savings on retail and leisure.
- Company pension scheme

If your application is successful, you will be contacted within 5 working days. If you do not hear from us after 5 working days you have not been successful on this occasion and unless otherwise advised, Recruitment Pro will keep your details on file to contact you regarding any future suitable opportunities.

title: Traffic Process Administration Assistant
description:
Adecco are pleased to be recruiting for a Traffic Process Administration Assistant to work within the Lincolnshire Police Force

Location: Nettleham, Lincoln
Contract Type: Temporary
Hourly Rate: 12.83 per hour
End Date: May 2027
Working Pattern: Full Time 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday 8am to 4.30pm

Our client, a leading organisation within the public services sector, is seeking a dedicated and detail-oriented Traffic Process Administration Assistant to join their Criminal Justice Services Traffic Process Unit. This is an exciting opportunity to play a vital role in supporting various internal and external partners, including the Lincolnshire Road Safety Partnership and His Majesty's Courts and Tribunal Service.

Key Responsibilities:
- Provide high-quality administrative support, ensuring seamless communication with police officers, the Crown Prosecution Services (CPS), and other stakeholders.
- Administer officer-issued tickets, process notices of intended prosecution for speeding offences, and manage files related to road traffic collisions.
- Maintain and quality control data on police systems, ensuring accuracy and compliance with policies.
- Liaise with members of the public via telephone and email, offering guidance and support as needed.
- Create and maintain electronic case files, ensuring all documentation meets national and local quality standards.
- Respond to inquiries from partner agencies, solicitors, and insurance companies, providing necessary advice and information.
- Attend court as required and support other units within the Criminal Justice Services when necessary.

What Our Client Is Looking For:

Qualifications/Training:
- Understanding of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and GDPR/DPA legislation (Desirable).
- Knowledge of police computer systems and administrative procedures (Essential).
Experience:
- Proven experience in data input and retrieval within an administrative role (Essential).
- Familiarity with a computerised department (Desirable).
Skills:
- Excellent written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills (Essential).
- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities (Essential).
- Demonstrated ability to ensure a high degree of accuracy in information handling (Essential).
Motivation/Commitment:
- Ability to work independently and use initiative effectively (Essential).

Why Join Our Client?
This role offers the chance to contribute meaningfully to public service, working in a supportive environment that values professionalism and integrity. With a competitive hourly rate and the opportunity for career development, this position is perfect for those passionate about making a difference.

If you thrive in a fast-paced environment and have a keen eye for detail, this could be the perfect role for you. Don't miss out on the chance to be part of an organisation committed to delivering high standards of service.

How to Apply:
Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications as soon as possible. This is a fantastic opportunity to join a dynamic team and contribute to the essential work of our client.

title: Account Coordinator
description:
Join the Stafforce Team

At Stafforce, we're passionate about connecting people with opportunities and helping our clients build reliable, skilled workforces. We are looking for a proactive and organised Candidate Consultant (Account Coordinator) to join our team on a temporary basis, supporting a number of key client accounts across the Scunthorpe area.
This is a varied, fast-paced role where no two days are the same. You'll play a vital part in the candidate journey, from sourcing and onboarding workers through to supporting their assignments and ensuring our clients receive an outstanding service.

The Role

As a Candidate Consultant, you will work closely with our recruitment and account management teams to support the delivery of temporary workforce solutions. You will be responsible for coordinating worker onboarding, conducting inductions, maintaining accurate records, and ensuring workers are fully supported throughout their employment.
This role is primarily office-based but will involve travel to client sites across the Scunthorpe area to support onboarding and workforce activities.
The standard working hours are 8:30am to 5:00pm, Monday to Friday, however flexibility is essential as some client requirements may require early starts. You will also participate in an out-of-hours and weekend on-call rota to support our clients and workforce when needed.
This is a temporary position, initially offered for a fixed-term period, with the potential for extension depending on business requirements.

Key Responsibilities
- Support recruitment activities by sourcing and coordinating suitable candidates.
- Conduct candidate registrations and onboarding processes.
- Deliver worker inductions and site briefings.
- Complete compliance checks, right-to-work verification, and employment documentation.
- Maintain accurate records using Stafforce's internal systems and databases.
- Update and manage workforce data using Microsoft Excel and other software packages.
- Build strong relationships with candidates, workers, clients, and colleagues.
- Monitor worker attendance and assist with shift coordination.
- Support workforce planning and fulfil client staffing requirements.
- Resolve worker queries and provide ongoing support throughout assignments.
- Ensure all processes are completed accurately and in line with company procedures.
- Participate in the out-of-hours and weekend on-call rota.
- Travel between client sites and offices as required.

What We're Looking For
Essential Skills & Experience
- Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
- Strong IT and administrative skills.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
- Confident using databases, software systems, and Microsoft Office applications.
- Excellent organisational skills with strong attention to detail.
- Ability to prioritise workload and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
- Strong customer service and relationship-building skills.
- A flexible and positive approach to work.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Desirable Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in recruitment, account coordination, administration, customer service, or a similar role.
- Experience working with temporary workers or within high-volume staffing environments.
- Full UK driving licence due to travel requirements across multiple client locations in the Scunthorpe area.

What You'll Receive

In return, Stafforce offers a supportive environment where you can develop your skills and make a real difference to both candidates and clients.

Benefits Include:
- Competitive salary of 27,700 per annum (pro rata for the duration of the temporary contract).
- Full training and ongoing development opportunities.
- Valuable experience within a well-established and growing business.
- 24/7 GP access through our employee wellbeing programme.

title: Receptionist
location: Cleethorpes, DN35 7XE, GRIMSBY, DN31 2BH, Grimsby, DN31 3AE, CLEETHORPES, DN35 0LN
description: This is not a basic receptionist role - you will be doing more than greeting people and advising they are here. The role is fast paced and can be challenging. It requires a person who has an good eye for detail, can be empathetic, firm but fair. The majority of the work is in a small call centre or front desk of the respective practice. You will be trained in the practice protocols which you will be required to adhere to when answering the incoming messages, calls and visits. The candidate will be working across various sites on a rota basis so transport would be adventagous but not essential. The current team have a good repore so we are looking for a character who will fit in well and be as valued as the current staff are. Answering calls and message requests from patients, carers and outside agencies - arranging appointments, tests and ongoing care with services outside of the practice and responding with the correct information in a timely and professional manner. This role requires team work as well as initiative to problem solve on the go. Liasing and relaying information accurately between GP's, clinical teams and the general public is a must. A background of customer service would be an advantage but common sense and politeness are essential. PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBLITIES: To act as first point of contact and representative for the practice either by telephone or face to face. Liaise with all groups including but not exclusive to patients, trade people, pharmacies, clinical staff, outside providers Welcome visitors by greeting them, in person or on the telephone, answering or referring inquiries. Direct visitors by maintaining employee and department directories; giving instructions. Maintain security by following procedures, monitoring logbooks. Booking appointments and signposting patients to the correct services to enable self-care, over the phone and face to face at the reception desk Producing the appointment and information letters / leaflets for service users. Ensuring the front reception is clean, tidy, and professional in appearance. Keeps medical office supplies adequately stocked by anticipating inventory needs, placing orders, and monitoring office equipment. Be aware of personal, practice and patient safety. Use conflict resolution skills as required and know where the panic alarms are and how to respond should on go off. Actively running the diary by booking, moving, changing, and arriving patient. Facilitates patient flow by notifying the clinicians of patients' arrival, being aware of delays, and communicating with patients and clinical staff. Ensuring any DNA patients are sent a text and followed up, especially children with safeguarding in mind. Giving advise on partner services for patients to be able to contact such as pharmacy minor ailments and physio, Push Doctor etc. Be able to use the system one application to amend patient information, issue prescriptions, issue online access logins and update records appropriately. Updating patient demographics by collecting the information at each contact. Protect patient confidentiality. Add appropriate home visits along with information for clinical team. Be able to amend and add information such as BP and smoking statuses to QOF requirements. Entering accurate, relevant, concise data/details into the patient record and transferring messages to the appropriate person through nominated pathways i.e., task. Completing returned task requests, and relaying accurate information to nominated people. Re-visiting computerised records to ensure accuracy of information entered. Use accurx to full potential by sending/ requesting information and dealing with responses succinctly. Know how to find pathology and radiology results, respond appropriately to patient or Clinical staff with results. Know how to utilise systems (following training) for patients on INR and advise, record and complete appropriately. Using NHS Email communication system and ensuring this is checked regularly as this is an inhouse communication method. Recording outgoing documents and processing small amounts of cash handling, recording these appropriately. Assisting with incoming processing of prescriptions via all medium of receipt (post, electronic, telephone etc) to include booking of monitoring bloods when required, passing to the appropriate team for amending/adding of medication and assisting with the monthly recalls for vulnerable patient prescriptions. Assisting with the printing of repeat prescriptions, ensuring security and compliance to practice policy for collection and safety of prescriptions. All these processes will be overviewed by the GPs for assurance and safety. Updating patient records with nominated pharmacy, including out of area holiday requests. Liaising with the District Nurses and other clinicians to ensure housebound patients are reviewed. Sending appropriate electronic referrals. Upholding the practice policies and guidance on Confidentiality, Health and Safety, Infection control and equality and diversity. Completion of mandatory training in a timely manner, ensuring updated at appropriate time periods and attendance on a minimum basis of two staff meetings per annum. (Where off duty this will be reimbursed). Receive incoming calls and messages presented via Emma AI assistant which will require you to respond, and allocate as needed to assist the patient. Answering the phone while maintaining a polite, consistent phone manner, on both the appointment line and the general enquiries line and directing calls appropriately. This is a high pressure, fast paced role that requires quick thinking and empathy whist adhering to protocols where a polite manner is needed to reassure the caller, they are being cared for to the best of the practices ability. will cover completion of reception task inbox, daily DNA s, seasonal campaigns, Qof recalls, patient reminders for appointments, surveys. Registering patients and collating the appropriate documents for this purpose. Be able to use remote booking system for services run by the practice at alternative locations. Record a pregnancy or death and inform appropriate team. Have an all-round understanding of QOF and the required appointments. Any other duties as may be delegated. The Operations Manager reserves the right to alter or amend this job description in consultation with the post holder.

title: Receptionist
description: The GP receptionist is responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and providing support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties may include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of personal information and assisting patients as required. To act as a central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with the multidisciplinary team member and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The core responsibilities of the receptionist are as follows. On occasion, there may be a requirement to carry out tasks not listed below, that are within the reasonable scope of the role. Maintain and monitor practice appointment system Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as requested Input data as necessary onto patients healthcare records Direct requests for information to relevant team members i.e., SAR, DVLA forms, insurance/solicitors letters Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Carry out system searches as requested Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required Photocopy documentation as required Maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards In addition to the core responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to; 1. Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary 2. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the rota 3. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead 4. Support admin team, providing cover during absences 5. Scan patient related documents and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare record We currently have 2 part time vacancies available allowing us to be flexible for the right candidate. All hours will be worked between 08:00 and 18:30, Monday to Friday
